title: Robotic inguinal hernia repair (r‑TAPP). Video report and results of a series of 302 hernia operations
citation: Ramser M, et al. Chirurg. 2021. (English version available on PMC).
learningObjectives: Identify key posterior groin structures as they appear during rTAPP.
Place major steps of rTAPP into the correct sequence.
Translate dynamic appearance (tissue behavior) into stable anatomic understanding.
paperIn3MinBullets: Video article illustrating rTAPP anatomy and steps, paired with outcomes from a 302-hernia series.
Focus is on dynamic anatomy: what appears when, and how tissue behaves with traction and dissection.
Best used after at least one ‘map’ module (Furtado) so video reinforces an existing mental model.
Includes supplementary video (English version available on PMC).

pauses.prompt: What space is being entered here?
pauses.explanation: Use context: lateral dissection over iliopsoas/external iliac region.

pauses.prompt: Identify the landmark that orients the posterior view.
pauses.explanation: Inferior epigastrics are a key landmark for orientation.

activities.title: Order the rTAPP steps
activities.prompt: Drag the steps into the correct order (high-level).
activities.explanation: High-level sequencing for learners; paper/video provide the visual mapping.

flashcards.front: Why use video learning for rTAPP anatomy?
flashcards.back: It shows tissue depth, tension, and how landmarks ‘appear’ through the sequence—bridging atlas → OR.

flashcards.front: Best prerequisite module before this one:
flashcards.back: Furtado (orientation map) so you can recognize landmarks as they appear.
